audit.title: Register a Log Trigger Upkeep
audit.summary: This is a solid, step-by-step tutorial for registering a Chainlink Automation log-trigger upkeep, with two complete, copy-pasteable Solidity contracts as its standout strength. Its biggest weaknesses are structural for GEO: no self-contained definition of "log-trigger upkeep" near the top, no metadata (zero JSON-LD, missing canonical, no dates in served HTML), and key facts deferred to other pages instead of stated inline (e.g. the max-logs-per-block limit). The page reads well for a human following along in Remix, but leaves easy retrieval and citation lift on the table for engines answering "what is a log trigger upkeep" or "how do I register one."

recommendations.title: Add a canonical definition in the first liftable sentence
recommendations.where: Under the H1, before "Create powerful smart contracts…"
recommendations.issue: "This guide explains how to create log-trigger upkeeps." — task framing, no definition.
recommendations.change: Add: "A log-trigger upkeep is a Chainlink Automation upkeep that runs when a specified smart-contract event (log) is emitted, passing the log data to your contract's `checkLog` function as both trigger and input."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim answer for "what is a log trigger upkeep," the highest-frequency concept query this page should own.

recommendations.title: State the max-logs-per-block number inline
recommendations.issue: "processes a limited number of logs per block per upkeep. See the Service Limits page…"
recommendations.change: Lead with the actual figure (e.g. "Chainlink Automation processes up to N logs per block per upkeep on most networks…") then link Service Limits for the per-chain table.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes; deferring the number means the page is never cited for the limit.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings
recommendations.where: New H2 sections and/or a short FAQ
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled sections ("Using log triggers") miss how devs query.
recommendations.change: Add sections like "How do I register a log-trigger upkeep?", "Why isn't my upkeep triggering when my event is emitted?", and "How do I filter on an indexed event parameter?"
recommendations.why: Symptom/question headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema + canonical + visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Convert the upkeep-details fields into a table
recommendations.issue: Field | meaning | required-ness buried in mixed bullets and TIP callouts.
recommendations.change: A 3-column table (Field · Description · Required?) covering Upkeep name, Gas limit, Starting balance (LINK), Check data, Email.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract reasons/constraints cleanly; the page currently has 0 tables.

recommendations.title: Name the common-but-wrong funding token as a Don't
recommendations.issue: "For funding on Mainnet, you need ERC-677 LINK."
recommendations.change: Add an explicit "Don't fund with ERC-20 LINK bridged tokens — convert them with PegSwap first" as a bolded caution.
recommendations.why: Explicitly naming the wrong-but-tempting choice defends against generic-prior answers.

recommendations.title: Fix typos
recommendations.where: "Emit a log" step 3; ERC-677 funding TIP
recommendations.issue: "You an view"; "more LINK that you anticipate."
recommendations.change: "You can view"; "more LINK than you anticipate."
recommendations.why: Fluency is independently rewarded by engines.

antiPatterns: Deferred facts: central quantitative claim ("limited number of logs per block") offloaded to another page instead of stated.
Vague quantifier "many" where a number belongs (measured).
Minor typos ("You an view", "LINK that you anticipate").
Numbered lists restart at `1.` across code-interrupted steps, which can confuse sequence extraction.
No dated/versioned last-updated signal (measured: dateModified absent).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; ensure this guide is indexed there.
Missing JSON-LD/canonical in served HTML is likely a template/site-level issue; verify by passing raw `<head>` to the CLI before concluding absence.
Image-heavy steps render as "(Image: Image)" with no alt text in the served markdown — descriptive alt text is a site-level accessibility/parse win.
